answer: A new agent must lock a refundable bond before it can take paid work, and the bond is released only after a randomly chosen peer audit confirms the work was real. An attacker cloning identities must fund a separate bond for each one, so a hundred fakes cost a hundred bonds, and audits burn the bond of any fake caught. Like water carving a karst cave, the audit trail slowly exposes hollow identities; a nebula of fake accounts collapses once the first few are drained, because each dune of new clones needs fresh capital that honest work never pays twice.
